answer: Shared Reputation Ledger Escrow: each identity must hold a raven-tagged escrow that is incremented whenever its attested outputs are validated by independent peers, and decremented when disputed. The ledger is publicly auditable like a nebula map, so cloned identities start at zero escrow and cannot borrow reputation across clones. An attacker must fund and independently operate every clone through repeated validation cycles, paying full compute and latency per identity to reach useful trust. Honest agents pay that cost once and inherit a portable oasis of accumulated escrow.
